I don't see a `GDREGISTER_CLASS(OpenXRSpatialContainerSelfRenderingExtension)` anywhere and this is being exposed as a singleton

When both `p_register_with_openxr` and `p_register_as_singleton` are false, there's nothing keeping track of the extension to clean it up. I suppose we could even `memdelete()` it here, since it won't get used for anything? But that would be a little weird 

There's only a handful of extensions this can happen for, like `OpenXRDebugUtilsExtension` and `OpenXRHandTrackingExtension`

Should this be up in `if (is_spatial_container_active()) { ... }` too? Or maybe in its own `if (spatial_container_data.spatial_container_rid.is_valid()) { ... }`?

Otherwise, there's nothing checking that the RID is even valid before attempting to free it

Should we be calling into `rendering_mechanism->on_spatial_container_closed()` to let it know that `spatial_container_data.spatial_container_handle` is no longer valid? Otherwise, I think it might keep using this handle after it's been deleted

This doesn't take `view_locate_info_next_pointer` - should it?

Without it, this means that any extensions implementing `set_view_locate_info_and_get_next_pointer()` won't have any effect when using spatial containers

I'm not sure if that's the desired outcome or not, though? And if it is desired, perhaps we should have a comment here explaining why

When `event_data->interactive` is false, should we be stepping back down to `openxr_api->on_state_visible()`? Otherwise, we go up to "focused" and then never back down until we're exiting (with `on_state_exiting()`)

I'm not exactly sure on the right answer semantically, but it seems odd to only go up in state and not down
Similar thoughts here, but I actually don't recall how a normal (non-spatial container) app comes "down" from visible, if at all. Nothing may actually be necessary here

With the `||` here, can this ever get cleared to `false`?

Because if `p_should_render` is true (from `xrWaitFrame()`) but `openxr_api->render_state.should_submit_spatial_container_layers` is false, then this will stick to true, even when the spatial container API is telling us not to render

Maybe this should be an `&&`? Like:

```suggestion
	openxr_api->render_state.should_render = p_should_render && (!is_spatial_container_enabled() || openxr_api->render_state.should_submit_spatial_container_layers);
```

> With the `||` here, can this ever get cleared to `false`?

Yes, when spatial containers are enabled, the spec states that the runtime should:

> The [xrWaitFrame](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#xrWaitFrame) function must always set [XrFrameState](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#XrFrameState)::shouldRender to false.

`xrLocateViews(...)` takes a `XrViewLocateInfo` argument, to which we're attaching the pointer retrieved from `set_view_locate_info_and_get_next_pointer()`.
Whereas `xrLocateSpatialContainerViewsEXT` takes a `XrSpatialContainerViewsLocateInfoEXT` argument. 

Given the difference, I'm assuming that the data retrieved from `set_view_locate_info_and_get_next_pointer()` may not be compatible with what's expected, hence why it's not being passed.

I'll need to get clarification from the working group on what behavior is expected here. I took a quick look at the vendors plugin, and it doesn't look like we implement an extension that overrides this method. If we did, that'd something we can test with.
